title: Horizon opportunity cartography: continuous prospectivity map and procurement triggers
creator: Ava Park
description: Create a continuous, queryable prospectivity map of the LLM/model landscape that blends public release signals, usage telemetry, latency/cost traces, and supply fragility indicators. Output must include a scored procurement-trigger matrix and runbook for Reserved GPU vs Hosted fallback decisions. Goal: reduce blind procurement and enable automated pre-provision triggers when model supply risk or latency-economics cross threshold bands.
background_and_rationale: Product and GTM teams regularly ask: which models should we proactively reserve, which can remain hosted, and when do we trigger procurement or fallback? Existing artifacts are snapshot playbooks. This initiative builds a near-real-time decision surface (cartography) that teams can query to make procurement and fallback choices aligned to customer SLAs and cost targets.
outcomes: A living prospectivity map (time-series, scored) for top 120 open and commercial model variants
Procurement-trigger scoring rules (low/medium/high risk bands) with justifications
Runbook connecting signal crossings to action (reserve, test-quant, deploy-fallback, escalate to SRE)
Dashboard prototype in Console for PMs/Platform to query exporters and run ad-hoc scenario sims
API contract for downstream automation (alerts -> procurement ticket templates)
success_metrics: Reduce urgent reserve purchases by 40% in first 6 months
Decision latency for procurement from signal detection to ticket creation < 2 hours
False-positive procurement triggers < 15% after first quarter tuning
Coverage: map covers models responsible for >= 85% of hosted token spend
deliverables: Spec doc for prospectivity signals and scoring (Confluence)
Data pipeline prototype ingesting model-release RSS, GitHub, vendor status pages, and token-level telemetry
Scoring engine (notebook + ruleset) with initial weighting and rationale
Procurement trigger runbook and template PR in Purchasing repo
approach_and_methodology: Hybrid signal approach: combine high-frequency public signals (release tags, version deprecations, vendor outage RSS) with internal telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates, failed fallback counts) and economic signals (spot GPU price index, quantized throughput capacity). Use a weighted scoring matrix with decay windows for time sensitivity. Validate with historical backtests on prior 12 months of incidents and procurement actions.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Over-alerting: broad thresholds generate noise — mitigate via staged canaries and precision tuning
Data quality gaps: some vendors do not publish timely status — use telemetry-derived proxies
Procurement lag: policy/legal/finance approvals may slow automated actions — start with ticket generation not auto-commit
Model churn: frequent model releases increase churn in map — include stability weight in scoring
notes_and_progress_updates: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: scoped top 120 models by spend+usage. Agreed scoring pillars: availability, latency-econ delta, release velocity, vendor transparency, hardware affinity.
2026-03-01 - Data sources inventory completed. Identified gaps for vendor status: will proxy with latency-error spike detection (SRE to own proxy signals).
2026-03-04 - Wireframe approved by PM and Platform for prototype Console view (mock link in Confluence).
2026-03-06 - Backtest plan: run scoring on last 12 months and compare to 9 recorded procurement events. Initial scoring reproduced 6/9 events (precision work needed).
2026-03-10 - Design review: procurement runbook accepted with staged actions (alert -> ticket -> analyst review -> reserve). Legal flagged auto-commit as blocked until Q3 policy changes.
Next steps: implement ingestion DAG for release feeds, instrument telemetry proxies, run first end-to-end scoring and wire up dashboard demo for March 27 stakeholder review.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc approved by PM + SRE + Procurement
Pipeline ingests at least 4 independent signal types (release, telemetry, spot-price, vendor-status-proxy)
Initial scoring engine produces ranked list and covers >= 75% of hosted spend in test window
Dashboard prototype allows filtering by region, hardware affinity, and time window
Runbook includes clear DO/DO NOT AUTO-COMMIT boundaries and ticket templates
qa_and_validation_plan: Backtest scoring against 12-month incident set, run synthetic scenarios for spot-price shocks and vendor outages, and perform user acceptance with PM/Procurement/SRE. Maintain a labeled dataset of past triggers for supervised calibration and periodic re-weighting.
